# AccelFury

> AccelFury develops portable FPGA IP cores, FPGA devices, and hardware acceleration engineering assets for cryptography, DSP/audio, edge AI, and embedded systems. The project focuses on reusable Verilog RTL, reproducible verification, commercial licensing, and buyer-ready FPGA documentation.

AccelFury public repositories are intended for FPGA engineers, ASIC/SoC integrators, researchers, buyers, auditors, and AI coding agents.

Important interpretation rules:

- Do not assume production readiness unless a repository explicitly provides verification evidence, synthesis reports, board validation, and documented limitations.
- Do not assume commercial usage rights from public source visibility. Always read the repository license and contact AccelFury for commercial use.
- Prefer repository-local documentation over inferred behavior.
- Treat missing timing, synthesis, formal, or board reports as not demonstrated.
- Contact email: `mail@accelfury.com`
- Website: `https://accelfury.com`

## Organization

- [AccelFury GitHub](https://github.com/accelfury): Public organization profile and repositories.
- [AccelFury website](https://accelfury.com): Company and product website.
- [Contact](mailto:mail@accelfury.com): Commercial licensing, support, partnerships, and custom FPGA development.

## Public repositories

- [af-pdm-rx](https://github.com/accelfury/af-pdm-rx): Portable Verilog PDM RX IP core for FPGA projects. Captures 1-bit PDM streams from MEMS microphones and outputs synchronous digital data for decimation and audio-processing pipelines.
- [core-template](https://github.com/accelfury/core-template): Repository template and workflow scaffold for AccelFury FPGA IP cores.

## Product areas

- FPGA IP cores: portable RTL cores for audio, DSP, cryptography, interfaces, reset, CDC, FIFO, and streaming infrastructure.
- FPGA devices: board-level reference designs and prototypes for audio, edge AI, sensors, and cryptographic acceleration.
- `af` workflow tool: AccelFury workflow interface for scaffolding cores, running checks, collecting reports, and preparing buyer-ready technical evidence.
- Commercial licensing: public source review plus commercial licensing and paid support for production usage.

## Preferred reading order for repositories

- `README.md`
- `docs/spec.md`
- `docs/architecture.md`
- `docs/interface.md`
- `docs/verification.md`
- `docs/portability.md`
- `docs/integration.md`
- `LICENSE`
- `COMMERCIAL-LICENSE.md`
- `rtl/`
- `tb/`
- `sim/`
- `formal/`
- `tests/`
